title: You’re Not Thinking Big Enough: Rebuilding Food Systems with AI Agents — Cody Menefee, Firecrawl
talk_summary: A Firecrawl growth-team talk proposing LLM-driven pasture rotation for grass-fed livestock, where an LLM reasons over GPS, grass height, drought, and biodiversity data to suggest where to move herds, gated by open collar APIs and a scraped knowledge base. It is mostly a domain pitch and hiring ad, with no agent-orchestration engineering results.

takeaways.technique: Scrape domain knowledge into an open knowledge base for agent grounding
takeaways.what_they_do: They scrape YouTube videos and research papers with Firecrawl into an open-source repo (Open Pasture) so an LLM has domain context to reason over.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the number one problem is actually just giving the agents the context they need, gathering the data, packaging that data

takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM makes a non-deterministic multivariate recommendation that a human can confirm or deny, rather than being forced into a deterministic pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: drop an LLM in the center to actually reason over the data and at least make a suggestion that the human can confirm or deny
